Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.ruling: STRUCTURAL, not recall tail. Three independent lines converge, and NONE of them is management characterisation.
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.line_1_geography: The Acton plant ships pods to BOTH geographies. A reliability-driven attrition break must appear in both. It does not: international was RAISED 400bp and printed +32.9% cc. The recall-attrition hypothesis is REFUTED by its own required signature. (This is the prior court's 'genuine update against the kill' - correct observation, but it exonerates the DEFECT, not the BUSINESS.)
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.line_2_first_principles: Mode B, no promoter framing: why would a T2D patient quit a pump inside 90 days when a T1D patient does not? Because the counterfactual differs. For T1D, the alternative to a pod is 4-5 injections/day of a therapy that is mandatory for survival - discontinuation is near-unthinkable, which is why Omnipod's historical persistence is structurally high. For a basal-insulin T2D patient the alternative is ONE injection a day, or increasingly a GLP-1. Wearing a device 24/7, changing it q3d, and paying a copay for a marginal A1c benefit is a discretionary purchase. High early discontinuation is not a defect in the product OR in the execution - it is the underlying economics of the segment, and it was always going to be true. What broke is the ASSUMPTION that the T2D TAM converts at T1D-like persistence. That assumption is what the growth premium was built on.
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.line_3_timing: See Q2b. The audited customer-acquisition metric turned down in Q1-2026, i.e. BEFORE the March 12 recall was initiated. An acquisition slowdown that pre-dates the recall cannot be the recall's tail.
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.consequence: This matters because the two hypotheses have opposite durations. Recall attrition is a bounded one-time cohort loss that laps in four quarters. A lower steady-state T2D persistence rate permanently lowers net-adds per gross-add, permanently raises acquisition cost per retained patient, and permanently shrinks the marketed TAM. The market spent today pricing the first; the evidence supports the second. So: 2027 mid-teens is more likely a WAY STATION than a floor.
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.t1d_franchise_read: INTACT, with the caveat that no T1D-specific metric is published. Support: international (overwhelmingly T1D) accelerating to 30-32% cc; total Q2 beat the high end; Spain is the 26th country / 20th Omnipod 5 market so the international runway is real and multi-year. The impairment is to the NEW growth layer, not the core.
Q2_recall_tail_vs_structural_THE_DISCRIM.MODE_B_KICKER_the_less_priced_risk: The tape spent today on T2D. The bigger un-priced risk is the competitive clock, and it lands in exactly the window the 2027 guide covers: Tandem tubeless Mobi targeted 2H-2026, Medtronic MiniMed Fit submission fall-2026, Beta Bionics Mint ~Q2-2027. Omnipod's entire moat is being the ONLY tubeless pump. Recall-damaged reliability perception is nearly costless while there is nowhere to switch TO; it becomes expensive the moment there is. Recall and competition are MULTIPLICATIVE, not additive, and they compound in 2027 - and none of it is in the mid-teens number.

Q2b_NEW_FINDING_the_prior_unobservabilit.what_the_prior_court_ruled: 2026-07-02 red team, accepted as 'the decisive finding': 'NO new-start/attrition/utilization/channel-inventory metric exists anywhere in the 10-K/10-Q, so new-starts-intact is knowable ONLY from management verbal commentary.' That ruling drove the CSP-only downgrade and today's PASS.
Q2b_NEW_FINDING_the_prior_unobservabilit.that_ruling_is_wrong: A quantitative new-customer metric IS disclosed, quarterly and audited. 10-K Note 4 / 10-Q Note 2, 'Revenue and Contract Acquisition Costs': 'The Company incurs commission costs to obtain a contract RELATED TO NEW CUSTOMER STARTS. These costs are capitalized as contract assets... amortized... over the expected period of benefit... periodically reviewed for impairment.' The note gives the net balance (split across two captions) and the period amortization every quarter. Gross additions = dEnd-Begin + amortization. Gross additions are, by the company's own definition, dollars of commission paid to acquire NEW CUSTOMERS.

series_derived_from_primary_filings_USDm.method_validation: Two independent reconciliations tie exactly: FY24 = (60.9-48.6)+18.2 = 30.5 = sum of quarters; FY25 = (78.4-60.9)+22.7 = 40.2 = sum of quarters. The roll-forward is arithmetically exact, not an estimate.

what_it_says.it_is_a_faithful_proxy: FY24 -> FY25 gross additions +31.8% against FY25 revenue +30.7%. The metric tracked the top line to within ~1pp over a full year. That is the validation that licenses using it.
what_it_says.then_it_broke: Q1-26 gross additions $5.0M vs Q1-25 $9.3M = -46.2% y/y, in a quarter when reported revenue grew +33.9% and management RAISED guidance. $5.0M is below every quarter of 2025 and below Q2/Q3/Q4-2024; it is back to Q1-2024 levels ($4.5M) on a revenue base ~60% larger.
what_it_says.smoothed_for_lumpiness: Quarterly additions are lumpy (Q1-24 4.5 vs Q2-24 7.9), so the honest cut is TTM: 35.3 (Mar-25) -> 36.8 -> 38.0 -> 40.2 (Dec-25) -> 35.9 (Mar-26). TTM gross additions ROLLED OVER for the first time in the series, -10.7% off the Dec-25 peak, while TTM revenue was still compounding >30%.
what_it_says.the_confound_cuts_the_same_way: Balance fell 78.4 -> 77.1. Additions = dEnd-Begin + amortization + IMPAIRMENT. If part of the decline was an impairment of previously capitalised acquisition cost, then additions were higher than $5.0M - but an impairment means the company concluded acquired customers will not deliver the expected period of benefit, i.e. early churn. Both branches are the same bearish story. The finding is robust to its own main confound.
what_it_says.timing_is_the_kill: Q1-2026 ended March 31. The first cannula recall was initiated March 12 (openFDA, event_date_initiated 2026-03-12). The acquisition slowdown is substantially PRE-recall. This is the third independent refutation of the recall-tail hypothesis and the strongest support for the structural read.

Q2b_NEW_FINDING_the_prior_unobservabilit.evidence_grade: The arithmetic is CONFIRMED (audited balances, exact roll-forward, two-way reconciliation). The interpretation is PLAUSIBLE-strong, not CONFIRMED - see UNVERIFIABLE for the commission-rate confound.

MICROSTRUCTURE_MECHANISM_encode_this.masking_channel: The decisive operating metric (new patient starts) is not published as a KPI and management is not asked to characterise it. It survives only as a dollar balance of capitalised sales commissions, split across two balance-sheet captions, inside a revenue-recognition footnote, recoverable only by a three-period roll-forward against a separately-stated amortisation sentence. Nothing is concealed; it is disclosed in a form no screen reads.
MICROSTRUCTURE_MECHANISM_encode_this.signal_channel: 10-Q Note 'Revenue and Contract Acquisition Costs' -> capitalized contract acquisition costs, net (2 captions) + period amortization. ASC 340-40 mandates this for anyone who capitalises commissions, so the detector GENERALISES to any consumable/subscription medtech that refuses to publish patient counts (DXCM, TNDM, IRTC, and the SaaS complex).

T2D becomes a real but slower/smaller layer; international carries 25-30% for two-plus years on a 26-country footprint; US settles low-double-digit; ~70bp/yr margin expansion. scenarios_honestly_derived.bull_193: p 0.18. The T2D issue is patient-selection/onboarding/payer friction (fixable); 2027 cohorts retain better; Omnipod 6 (STRIVE, ADA 2026) and the fully-closed-loop programme (EVOLUTION 3) re-accelerate; guide proves conservative. FY27 adj EPS $8.76 at 22x. DELIBERATELY CAPPED AT 22x, NOT 25-28x: the prior red team killed the 28x re-rate on the DXCM precedent, and the tape below proves the point - DXCM is still -27% vs its pre-cut price two years on despite +32% revenue. Post-cut medtech multiples do not re-rate quickly. The right tail is capped by history, not by conservatism.
scenarios_honestly_derived.upside_to_e_fv: +8.8% over ~12 months from $132.32 - AT OR BELOW cost of equity. Probability-weighted, PODD is roughly FAIRLY VALUED here.
scenarios_honestly_derived.payoff_shape_is_the_verdict: Fat left tail (-24% to bear), capped right tail (+46% to bull, cap historically enforced by the DXCM precedent). Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.solving_the_tape_for_implied_weights: CORRECTED IN COURT (first solve was wrong and is not preserved as fact). With bear 100 / base 165 / bull 193, E = 165 - 65*p_bear + 28*p_bull. Setting E = 132.32 and holding p_bull at the tape-like 0.05 gives p_bear = 0.524, p_base = 0.426. Verify: 0.524*100 + 0.426*165 + 0.05*193 = 132.34. So the market implies roughly 52% bear / 43% base / 5% bull.
Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.but_the_disagreement_is_a_MULTIPLE_call_: Independent cross-check from the option surface: annual IV 47.1%, so P(price < $100 in 12 months) = N(ln(100/132.32)/0.471) = N(-0.595) ~ 28%, and P(< $116) ~ 39%. Our p_bear of 0.40 sits ON the vol surface's own implied probability of finishing in bear territory. We do NOT disagree with the market about the odds of a bad outcome. The entire claimed edge lives in asserting a 20x base multiple where the tape embeds ~16x. A multiple assertion is the weakest form of edge and it should not be dressed up as a probability edge.
Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.what_IS_already_priced: At $132.32 the market pays 15.8x FY27E adj EPS for a 72%-gross-margin recurring-consumable franchise still growing mid-teens. That is a MATURE-MEDTECH multiple. The growth premium is entirely gone - PODD has already been re-rated to its terminal state. Practical consequence: the remaining downside requires the NUMBERS to break further, not the multiple to compress further. Multiple risk is largely spent; earnings risk is not.

THE_DECISIVE_PRECEDENT_tape_verified.source: IBKR monthly bars, DXCM, 30 bars from 2022-11
THE_DECISIVE_PRECEDENT_tape_verified.path: Jun-2024 close $113.38. Jul-2024 (the guide-cut month): open 113.00, low 62.34, close 67.82 = -40%. Then Aug 69.34 / Sep 67.04 / Oct 70.48 / Nov 77.99 / Dec 77.77 / Jan-25 86.83 / Feb-25 88.37 - a +42% bounce off the cut-day trough within seven months. Then it RELAPSED: Mar-25 68.29 (-23%). Then a SECOND, DEEPER leg: Sep-25 67.29 / Oct-25 58.22, with the ultimate low $54.11 in NOVEMBER 2025. Recovery only from May-2026 (73.74) to today's 82.41.
THE_DECISIVE_PRECEDENT_tape_verified.the_three_numbers_that_matter: (1) The true post-cut trough came SIXTEEN MONTHS after the cut and was 13% BELOW the cut-day low. (2) A buyer of the cut-day close ($67.82) was underwater for roughly 22 months. (3) Two years on, DXCM is still -27% vs its pre-cut price DESPITE revenue growing ~32% over the same span - the entire residual loss is multiple, and it never came back.
THE_DECISIVE_PRECEDENT_tape_verified.read_across: This is the closest available comparable: same industry, same market-cap tier, same failure mode (US commercial execution plus guidance credibility, not product failure). The base rate says buying the guide-cut day on a decelerating diabetes-tech name returns approximately zero for ~2 years, with a ~20% interim drawdown below the entry, before it works. That single tape-verified precedent is a stronger argument against a day-0 entry than any valuation work in this record.
THE_DECISIVE_PRECEDENT_tape_verified.the_bounce_trap: Note especially the +42% seven-month bounce that then fully round-tripped. PODD already ran this play once - 138.79 (June) to 172.92 (late July, +25%) and back to 126.40 today. Expect more of them. A bounce is not a floor.

Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.where_the_disagreement_actually_sits: NOT where it first appeared. Our weights are 40/42/18 vs the market's ~52/43/5. The bear-weight gap is only 12pp; the BULL-weight gap is 13pp on a much smaller base - i.e. we are assigning 18% to an outcome the tape prices at ~5%. Essentially ALL of our positive expected value comes from that single bull weight, not from being less afraid of the downside.
Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.option_surface_cross_check_we_are_MORE_b: Independent check off the live vol surface (annual IV 47.1%, lognormal, no drift): P(price < $100 in 12 months) = N(ln(100/132.32)/0.471) = N(-0.594) = 27.6%. P(< $116) = 39.0%. Our bear weight of 40% on a $100 FV is therefore MORE pessimistic on the left tail than the options market, which assigns only ~28% to that zone. This matters and it cuts against us: we do not have a benign disagreement in which the market over-fears the downside. On the downside we agree with the market or exceed it. The entire claimed edge reduces to asserting an 18% bull probability where the tape says ~5% - and the bull case is precisely the one the DXCM tape shows is historically slow and capped, because post-cut medtech multiples do not re-rate for years. An edge that lives wholly in the least-likely, most-historically-suppressed branch is not an edge worth sizing.
Q4_how_much_bad_news_is_priced.caveat: Implied weights are solved on our own FV ladder and ignore drift and discounting; they are an internal-consistency device for reading the tape against our scenarios, not a market-quoted distribution.

Q5_ai_break_exposure.direct: NIL - CONFIRMED. Revenue is insulin-delivery consumables reimbursed by commercial insurers, Medicare and ex-US national health systems. The entry does NOT require the AI cycle to hold, and the de-rate prices nothing AI-related.
Q5_ai_break_exposure.second_order_and_it_nets_out: Two offsetting second-order effects, roughly cancelling: DEMAND is genuinely recession- and AI-cycle-insensitive (diabetics do not defer insulin), which is a mild hedge; but the equity is still a high-multiple growth stock whose multiple would compress with a broad risk-off, which is a mild beta. Net: no gating either way, and PODD should not be counted toward the ~$5.2M/26% AI-complex sleeve.

Q6_VERDICT.state: PASS - WATCH, dated reopen. No position (IBKR positions polled 2026-08-05: no PODD common, no PODD options; healthcare axis currently CI 34sh / HCA 12sh / ISRG 27sh / PRCT 25sh, small in dollars, so the axis cap is not the binding constraint - the name is).
Q6_VERDICT.de_rate_or_derailment: DERAILMENT. The contract's own frame is decisive: the winner pattern (HUBS/CTSH/SAP) is a multiple compressing on STABLE OR RISING estimates. Here estimates are falling and the multiple is following them down - FY26 US cut 300bp, FY27 re-based, Q4-26 US implied ~11.6%, and the audited acquisition metric turned down a quarter before any of it was disclosed. This is the pattern the frame exists to exclude.
Q6_VERDICT.response_taxonomy_classification: BUSINESS-RISK finding -> SIZE CUT / KILL. Explicitly NOT a valuation finding, so explicitly NOT a price gate. The prior court already made exactly this ruling when it voided the $138 limit ('a price gate is the instrument for a VALUATION concern; what arrived is a BUSINESS-RISK finding'). Nothing in today's data reverses it, and today's new finding STRENGTHENS it. Setting a fresh price gate now would repeat the identified error at a lower price.
Q6_VERDICT.edge_class: NO EDGE. Not RP_FAIR either - RP_FAIR requires fairness VERIFIED and tails BOUNDED. Fairness is approximately verified (E[FV] $144 vs $132.32), but the left tail is not bounded: it is governed by a 2027 competitive wave that is not in any published number and by a persistence assumption whose true value is unknown to us AND, on this evidence, was until recently unknown to management.
Q6_VERDICT.why_not_a_4_with_a_deep_band: Considered and rejected on three grounds, the third being structural. (1) Payoff shape: +8.8% to E[FV] with a -24% bear is not a rung-worthy asymmetry. (2) Path: day 0 of a new-low breakdown, and the DXCM base rate says the true trough is quarters away, not days. (3) CONTRACT RULE 5 - decisive. Any ladder here would be PULL-class, not ride-through: ride-through requires BOTH rungs anchored to court-blessed fair/bear value AND a named, OBSERVABLE kill branch governing the event. The kill branch for this name (are new starts stabilising?) is observable only in a 10-Q footnote roll-forward that lands AFTER the print it would need to govern. So the ladder would have to be pulled two sessions before every print - i.e. it can never be resting at the only moment that could fill it. A band that is structurally absent whenever it matters should not be written. Emitting one would be theatre.
Q6_VERDICT.what_would_change_this: Not a lower price. A demonstrated FLOOR under the growth rate. Concretely: two consecutive quarters of TTM capitalized-contract-acquisition additions no longer declining y/y, plus US Omnipod landing in-or-above its guided range twice, plus no third field action. On the DXCM template that is 3-6 quarters out, not one.
Q6_VERDICT.red_team_required: NO - score is below the >=6 threshold. Flagging instead for a DIFFERENT escalation (below), which is the higher-value use of the court's time.

ESCALATION_REQUESTED_not_a_red_team.what: The capitalized-contract-acquisition-cost roll-forward should be escalated as a NEW CROSS-VERTICAL DETECTOR, independent of the PODD verdict. Per the standing doctrine that a load-bearing finding gets re-verified with full context and a stronger model before it is relied on, and that agent-surfaced framework changes get WIRED IN rather than left as notes.
ESCALATION_REQUESTED_not_a_red_team.why_it_is_worth_it: It overturned an accepted 'decisive finding' (the prior red team's structural-unobservability ruling) using only audited primary filings; it validated against a full year of revenue (+31.8% vs +30.7%); it led price by ~13 weeks through a 17% counter-rally; and ASC 340-40 makes it MANDATORY disclosure for any issuer that capitalises sales commissions - so it generalises to every consumable-medtech and SaaS name that hides its customer counts.
ESCALATION_REQUESTED_not_a_red_team.proposed_contract: APPLIES_TO: any name where (a) the thesis depends on new-customer/new-patient/new-logo velocity AND (b) the issuer publishes no customer-count KPI AND (c) the filings contain a 'costs to obtain a contract' / contract-acquisition-cost note. Output: TTM gross additions, y/y, versus TTM revenue y/y. FIRE when TTM additions growth turns negative or falls more than ~15pp below TTM revenue growth.
ESCALATION_REQUESTED_not_a_red_team.known_limitations_to_test_before_promoti: Quarterly lumpiness is real (Q1-24 4.5 vs Q2-24 7.9) - TTM only. Cannot separate additions from impairment (both bearish here, but that may not hold on other names). Blends geographies and channels. Sensitive to commission-plan redesign, which is the one confound that could invert the reading entirely.

four_idea_frame.what_the_market_believes: Insulet's growth story is over. The recalls broke the reliability franchise, the T2D expansion that justified the premium was a mirage, three tubeless competitors arrive within a year, and mid-teens is the first stop on the way to single digits. Price it as mature medtech - 16x - and stop paying for growth.
four_idea_frame.what_we_believe: The market has the right conclusion for substantially the wrong reason. The recall did NOT break the franchise - the geography test refutes that cleanly, since Acton ships to both regions and international was RAISED to 30-32%. What actually broke is narrower and more durable: the assumption that type-2 patients persist like type-1 patients. That was never a defect story; it is the economics of selling a 24/7 wearable to a patient whose alternative is one injection a day or a GLP-1. The T1D core and the 26-country international runway are intact and genuinely undervalued at 2.9x sales; the T2D TAM that carried the premium is permanently smaller.
four_idea_frame.why_we_might_have_edge: We derived the acquisition slowdown from an audited quarterly footnote roll-forward that the market does not read and that our own prior court ruled did not exist. It flagged in the Q1-26 10-Q filed 2026-05-06 at ~$150 and led price by about a quarter, through a failed 17% rally. The same channel reads again within days, ahead of consensus, and it generalises well beyond this name.
four_idea_frame.why_it_might_be_priced_in: Because at 15.8x FY27 the multiple has ALREADY collapsed to its terminal state - the market did not need our footnote to reach the destination. Our own vol-surface cross-check puts the market's implied odds of a bear outcome at ~39%, essentially identical to our 40%. We do not out-forecast the market on probability here; we merely assert a 20x base multiple where the tape says 16x. That is a weak, assumption-driven edge, it is worth +8.8% before cost of equity, and it does not survive the DXCM base rate of ~22 months of dead money after a cut of exactly this kind.

HONESTY_READ.verdict: REVIEW_FLAG - unchanged in level from the prior record, and explicitly NOT an ELEVATE. No exclusion signal. This is a fundamental-analysis call, not a detector fire, and the record should say so plainly rather than borrow authority from the honesty framework.
HONESTY_READ.why_not_elevate: Per the standing boundary, grade takeaway-vs-data DIVERGENCE, not datum disclosure. Insulet cut the guide hard, re-based the out-year, and named the cause in the CEO's own quote on the day. A genuinely impaired business that discloses its impairment is CLEAN. Re-detecting honestly disclosed bad news is not the product.
HONESTY_READ.divergence_1_mild: 'While we are updating our outlook... our conviction in the long-term opportunity remains unchanged.' You cannot re-base 2027 AND hold that the long-term opportunity is unchanged; the re-basing IS a change in the long-term opportunity. Softening, not concealment.
HONESTY_READ.divergence_2_sharper: The headline takeaway 'we RAISED adjusted EPS growth to >30%' sits alongside H1 FCF falling 37% y/y and capex nearly doubling, and the adjustment excludes $36.7M of H1 medical-device-correction warranty cost that is real cash. The adjusted framing makes the print look better on cash than it is. This is the divergence most likely to mislead a headline reader, and it points the WRONG way for a buyer.
HONESTY_READ.divergence_3_carried_forward: The release again labels both actions 'Voluntary MDCs' where FDA's primary records classify them Class I recalls. Unchanged from the prior court's finding; noted, not re-litigated.
HONESTY_READ.net: Honest company delivering genuinely bad news, with characterisation-softening at the margins. The honesty channel gives no short signal and no exclusion here.

CONCESSION_1_my_headline_finding_is_DOWN.what_this_does_to_my_claim: I wrote that the audited contract-acquisition roll-forward showed 'the customer-acquisition engine broke.' Management discloses NEW CUSTOMER STARTS growing 20%+ y/y in BOTH geographies in Q2, from a second-highest-ever quarter. On the acquisition axis my strong reading is WRONG. The engine did not break.
CONCESSION_1_my_headline_finding_is_DOWN.also_the_prior_unobservability_ruling_fa: I refuted it via a footnote roll-forward. The cleaner refutation is that Insulet PUBLISHES NCS growth in its quarterly deck. The prior red team's ruling was scoped to 'anywhere in the 10-K/10-Q' - literally true, and that literal scoping is exactly what made it wrong. Lesson worth banking: an unobservability finding must be scoped to ALL disclosure vehicles (deck, call, IR site), not to SEC filings alone, or it manufactures a false blindness.
CONCESSION_1_my_headline_finding_is_DOWN.BUT_the_signal_was_real_and_I_mis-attrib: Reconciliation. Additions = dEnd-Begin + amortization + IMPAIRMENT. I flagged the impairment branch at court time as a confound and said both branches were bearish. With NCS at +20%, the impairment branch is now by far the more likely one: gross additions were probably fine (~$11M, consistent with 20% NCS growth) with roughly $6M of IMPAIRMENT on top, which is what made the net balance fall 78.4 -> 77.1. And impairment of capitalised customer-acquisition cost is the precise accounting fingerprint of NEWLY ACQUIRED COHORTS CHURNING BEFORE THE EXPECTED PERIOD OF BENEFIT - i.e. exactly the early-churn phenomenon management disclosed three months later on 2026-08-05.
CONCESSION_1_my_headline_finding_is_DOWN.net: The detector fired correctly and ~13 weeks early. My interpretation of WHICH mechanism it fired on was wrong. It is not an acquisition-velocity detector on this name; it is an EARLY-CHURN / retention detector operating through the impairment channel. That is a more precise and more valuable reading than the one I filed, and it is arrived at by conceding the contradiction rather than defending the original claim.
CONCESSION_1_my_headline_finding_is_DOWN.evidence_grade_revised: Arithmetic CONFIRMED (unchanged). CONCESSION_3_management_denies_the_cause.how_we_hold_this: Management's attribution (fixable execution/onboarding) and this court's first-principles attribution (structural T2D persistence economics) are genuinely COMPETING hypotheses and today's disclosure does not settle between them. CONCESSION_3_management_denies_the_cause.THE_90_DAY_FIGURE_IS_NOT_A_FIGURE: Decisive on sourcing: '90 days' appears only as a WINDOW, never as a rate. The 'Type 2 Patients Quit Before 90 Days' headline is editorial framing. Per the standing rule that verified is not guessed: this number must NOT be quoted as fact by us or by any red team.

ANALYTICAL_UPGRADE_it_is_a_LEAKY_BUCKET_.the_reframe: This is the most important thing the deck changes, and it is not in the direction of comfort. NCS is growing 20%+ y/y in both geographies while US revenue growth is guided down to ~11.6% in Q4-26. Acquisition is FINE; the installed base is LEAKING. For a razor-and-blade consumables annuity that is the worse of the two failure modes: it means lifetime value per acquired customer is FALLING, so the same 20% NCS buys less forward revenue each year, and acquisition dollars are being spent on cohorts that do not stay - which is precisely why capitalised acquisition cost would be impaired.
ANALYTICAL_UPGRADE_it_is_a_LEAKY_BUCKET_.why_this_matters_more_than_the_headline: A market that spent 2026-08-05 pricing 'growth is slowing' is pricing the wrong variable. Slower acquisition is cyclical and fixable with sales investment. Falling retention on newly acquired cohorts compounds against the installed base every quarter and degrades the terminal value that the whole multiple rests on. The deck's own words carry it: US 'continued NCS momentum' AND 'utilization/attrition trends below prior expectations'. Both halves are management's.
ANALYTICAL_UPGRADE_it_is_a_LEAKY_BUCKET_.effect_on_the_verdict: Reinforces PASS. It does not move E[FV] much - our scenarios were struck on revenue and margin, which already embed the net effect - but it upgrades the QUALITY of the bear case from 'growth decelerating for unclear reasons' to a named, mechanism-level impairment of unit economics, and it raises the bar for what a reopen must show. A reopen now requires evidence of RETENTION stabilising, not merely of revenue landing in a guided range.
